messages:
leah: Customer reports failures when model returns OpenAI-style enum values that don't match our tool schema. They get a 400 validation error from our tool runner. Posting minimal repro and logs they sent.

leah: Request they sent (trimmed):
```json
POST /v1/responses
{
  \"model\": \"gpt-openai-compat-1\",
  \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Send an urgent email to product@acme.com\"}],
  \"tools\": [{\"name\": \"send_email\", \"schema\": {\"type\": \"object\", \"properties\": {\"to\": {\"type\": \"string\"}, \"subject\": {\"type\": \"string\"}, \"priority\": {\"type\": \"string\", \"enum\": [\"low\", \"normal\", \"high\"]}}, \"required\": [\"to\", \"subject\"]}}]
}
```

leah: What the model returned (from our logs):
```json
{
  \"tool_call\": {
    \"name\": \"send_email\",
    \"arguments\": {\"to\": \"product@acme.com\", \"subject\": \"FYI\", \"priority\": \"urgent\"}
  }
}
```

leah: Error from runner: `400 tool_call_schema_mismatch - priority value \"urgent\" not in enum [low, normal, high]`

alex: This looks like an OpenAI-compat model using synonyms (urgent/high). We already saw similar with verbosity enums (short/concise vs low/medium/high). Is the customer using an OpenAI-exported tool schema or our tool registry?

leah: They registered the tool locally with our schema (above). The model is an OpenAI-compatible model that sometimes emits different enum values. Customer is hitting us because we validate strictly server-side.

maya: Quick questions: Do we preserve the model's raw tool_call payload anywhere upstream? Can we add a middleware that maps known aliases before JSON Schema validation?

ben: We do log the raw model output in the response event blob under `model_response_raw`. I can point you to the log id if needed. Mapping aliases is low-risk if we maintain a small canonical map for each tool enum. But we should be careful: mapping changes semantics.

alex: Repro steps I'd like: 1) Request id / response event id (we need the full model_response_raw) 2) Model name + model config (temperature, stop tokens) 3) Full tool schema used by customer (we have a trimmed one in ticket)

leah: Provided response id: `resp_20250318_9b2f`. Model: `gpt-openai-compat-1` with default sampling. Full tool schema attached to ticket.

support-bot: Incident note appended: `INC-9427 - openai-compat enum alias causing 400 on tool_call`

maya: Short-term workaround for customer: normalize on their side by mapping `urgent -> high`, `short -> low`, `concise -> low/medium` depending on context. Or set model to return structured args using our expected enum values via a system prompt: e.g. add to conversation: `Please use priority values exactly: low, normal, high.` That’s brittle but buys time.

alex: Medium-term: eng-ml + eng-platform add an opt-in compatibility layer that performs alias mapping before validation. We should keep a per-tool whitelist of allowed aliases and log mappings as warnings (not hard-fail).

ben: I can spike this as a feature flag on the tool runner: `openai_enum_compat=true` which applies a canonicalization map per tool. Will need tests for ambiguous mappings and audit logs.

leah: Customer-facing message drafted: "We identified that some OpenAI-compatible models return enum synonyms (e.g., \"urgent\" instead of \"high\"). We can: (a) advise a temporary client-side mapping, (b) add a system prompt to force specific enum tokens, or (c) enable an opt-in compatibility mode on our side. We're escalating to engineering and will update you within 48 hours."

alex: Assigning to eng-ml for mapping heuristics: alex -> PR for alias map + integration tests. eng-platform (ben) will add feature flag and telemetry.

leah: Ticket created: `SUP-7891`. ETA: spike + PR review in ~3 business days. I'll update customer now.

maya: Thanks — loop me in on the PR so we can align the recommended client workaround in our docs.

ben: Note: This also explains a few other small flurries of 400s in the past week that we couldn't repro — they were likely OpenAI-compat models with variant enums. Will add search across logs for `tool_call_schema_mismatch` + `priority` to find related incidents.

leah: Closing the loop here for now. Will post updates in thread when eng has PR/flag ready. :thumbsup:
